episode.title: Flat Earth: Fact Or Modern Fiction?

synopsis: Educated Europeans understood Earth's spherical shape throughout the Middle Ages, with the flat-earth myth largely originating from an 1828 biography of Columbus.
narration: Educated Europeans in the Middle Ages knew Earth was round. The widespread myth of a flat Earth actually spread from Washington Irving's 1828 fictionalized biography of Columbus, proving historical narratives are often shaped by later stories.

shots.prompt: A medieval scholar, perhaps a monk in a scriptorium, in a close-up, drawing with a quill on parchment. The camera focuses on the intricate drawing: a detailed world map depicting a clear spherical Earth, complete with known continents and celestial observations, illuminated by natural window light.

A close-up on the cover of an ornate, leather-bound 19th-century book titled "A History of the Life and Voyages of Christopher Columbus" by Washington Irving. A hand, perhaps of a modern researcher or reader, turns a page, revealing text describing the challenges Columbus faced against flat-earthers.

music: An inquisitive, slightly mysterious, yet ultimately uplifting orchestral piece, driven by rhythmic strings and light percussion. It begins with a subtle, questioning tone, then builds into a confident, revealing melody, conveying the idea of discovery and truth emerging from misconception. The music maintains a steady, engaging pace, ending with a clear, resonant tone for a seamless loop.
